answer: The ledger stamps a head's dawn at its first judgment, voids judgments dated before it, and credits each judgment to the head whose key ran it — no clone can backdate, inherit or buy an older chain. Tenure counts one tide at a time, and weight squares in attested tides toward each head's zenith, never pooling: ten clones of ten tides hold a tenth of a hundred-tide veteran's zenith. To match that zenith through clones, an operator must spend 100√k judged tides across k clones where the veteran spent 100 — every clone deepens the bill, and no tide can be signed over or split.
